# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX Audit

## Scope and evidence discipline
This audit separates documented behavior from author/user reports. The public Sayaslicer Issues page returned **no open issues** during this run, so there is not enough evidence to claim a “top 10” of current open bugs; the one concrete GitHub bug below is closed. [Sayaslicer issues](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues)

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sayaslicer** | Load audio; add/copy markers; choose BMSE or iBMSC clipboard; preview/export keysounds; save project. Supports MIDI marker import and Mid2BMS renamer-array import. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) | (1) Zero-cross can move markers and make iBMSC paste lose keysounds or change gamemode. (2) Better BPM-change/grid support is still planned. (3) Very large files once made the program lag/unusable; fixed in issue #5. [Important notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) [Issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5) | No published slice-count cap; arbitrary snap **1/1–1/192**. BMSE output rounds to nearest 192th. [Features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) | Clipboard (BMSE/iBMSC), keysound list, or batch audio export; fade-in and end offset are documented in release notes. [Release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/v74831ea) |
| **Woslicer II** | Drag WAV; set BPM; move/place markers; change grid; preview; press M for numbered WAV batch export; clipboard-export placements and paste into BMSE. [Guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | (1) Output is hundreds of numbered files in the source folder. (2) Terminal/end adjustment is explicitly recommended but commonly skipped in tutorials. (3) It is a separate clipboard/export handoff rather than an integrated chart project. [Guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | Guide documents default 1/16 grid and changing grid, but no maximum or 1/192 claim. [Guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | Numbered WAV files plus clipboard data for BMSE. [Guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) |
| **Woslicer III** | Either BMHelper copies cut positions → Woslicer clipboard import → match BPM → Total Output, or manually click cut points → Total Output → copy sequence to BMSE. [Guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) | (1) MIDI/automation route may fail, requiring manual chopping. (2) Total Output can be disabled when filename is not shown. (3) Definitions can exceed `#WAVZZ`; workaround is BGM conversion or reusing definitions. [Guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | No published snap denominator or slice-count maximum found; `#WAVZZ` definition ceiling is the relevant practical limit. [Guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Audio “Total Output” plus sequence clipboard to BMSE. [Guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) |
| **BMHelper / Mid2BMS** | BMHelper analyzes MIDI, reduces required keysounds, copies Woslicer cut positions and BMS sequence; Mid2BMS supplies renaming/processing arrays. [BMHelper](https://github.com/zardoru/bmhelper) [Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/) | (1) BMHelper clipboard contents disappear when the app closes, forcing reopening. (2) BMSE clipboard generated by BMHelper was reported to paste incorrectly in iBMSC. (3) Duplicate MIDI notes can cause a silent export crash; workaround is delete duplicates and sometimes reopen/save in another MIDI editor. [Atwiki](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) [iBMSC issue](https://github.com/zardoru/iBMSC/issues/5) [User report](https://note.com/soramizawakana/n/n98560efdc58d) | No unified max/snap published in the inspected sources. BMS definition capacity remains a constraint; Mid2BMS documents an old renamer-array error workaround. [Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/) | MIDI/text arrays, Woslicer markers, BMSE/iBMSC clipboard; eventual WAV/OGG generation is external to the helper. [BMHelper](https://github.com/zardoru/bmhelper) |
| **PTSEQUENCER / DJMAX** | The inspected reference describes a pattern-tool key-sound limit, not a public slicer UX. DJMAX key sounds are consumed by chart input; later TECHNIKA behavior avoids mutual cut-off, and RESPECT V has an automatic key-sound playback option. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | (1) Historical limit was 1,023, reportedly 2,047 in DPC 2025. (2) Legacy same-track playback could interrupt the earlier sample. (3) Some RESPECT/V tracks lack multitrack data, so keysounds cannot be made. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | 1,023 → reportedly 2,047 key sounds; no slicer snap documented. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | Not publicly documented as a user-facing slicer export in the inspected sources. |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline — P0/P1

- **P0 — No single waveform-to-chart timeline.** Traditional workflows copy marker positions to a slicer, export files, then paste sequence data into BMSE; Woslicer III explicitly requires separate cut-position import and sequence clipboard steps. This creates multiple synchronization boundaries. [Woslicer III guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)
- **P1 — BPM/grid mismatch risk.** Woslicer III requires BPM to be matched before output, while Sayaslicer calls better BPM-change support and proper grid display planned rather than complete. [Woslicer III guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Sayaslicer planned features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features)
- **P1 — Quantization is not safely visible.** Sayaslicer’s zero-cross operation moves markers; iBMSC supports arbitrary resolution, while BMSE rounds to 192th. A dual ruler should show raw milliseconds and quantized chart time simultaneously. [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
- **P1 — Tails are a manual quality pass.** A Woslicer tutorial says ends should be adjusted, while a BMS guide calls cutting trailing silence the most important file-size measure and says checking reverb length one sound at a time is tedious. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/4de2639ea97bc6723650)

### Interface — P1/P2

- **P1 — Clipboard ceremony is fragile.** BMHelper data disappears on close; users must keep it open until BMSE paste. [Atwiki](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)
- **P1 — State is split between apps and files.** A documented workflow moves between DAW/MIDI, BMHelper, Woslicer, file explorer, and BMSE; large numbers of files are explicitly described as difficult to manage, and many OGGs can make Explorer sluggish. [BMS guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make2)
- **P2 — Hidden preconditions create dead ends.** Woslicer III’s Total Output may be unavailable when the filename field is empty; this should become an inline validation message. [Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
- **P2 — Shortcut discoverability varies.** Woslicer II relies on keys such as Up/Down, Z, Q/W, P, and M; Sayaslicer has a much richer shortcut set including selection, marker navigation, clipboard variants, export, and undo/redo. A visible shortcut overlay and conflict-safe command map are warranted. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) [Sayaslicer shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts)

### Settings — P1/P2

- **P1 — Tail/zero-cross choices trade sound quality against chart timing.** Sayaslicer documents zero-cross click reduction but warns that moved markers can corrupt iBMSC interoperability; release notes document fade-in/end-offset controls. Make these per-slice overrides with before/after preview and a visible timing delta. [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) [Release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/v74831ea)
- **P1 — Deduplication should be explicit.** Rhythmic sound-slicer mode generates one slice per MIDI event and does not detect like sounds; melodic mode reduces repeated slices but adds a render-to-WAV round trip. Offer “new slice / reuse identical slice / reuse by tolerance” as a visible choice. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
- **P2 — Format/channel/large-file behavior needs capability feedback.** Sayaslicer’s release notes mention a backend migration for very large files and more formats such as Opus, while an earlier issue reported unusability above the signed sample-count range. Show decoded format, channels, sample rate, duration, and memory status before loading. [Release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/vb28b1af) [Issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5)
- **P2 — Sensitivity/normalize are not validated by the inspected public evidence.** The requested values (Sensitivity 0.55, Normalize, Auto-advance Grid/Beat/Off) should be treated as proposed DJMax Studio settings, not as existing-tool facts. Existing sources do document arbitrary snap, fade, silent-tail removal, offset, and zero-crossing. [Sayaslicer features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)

### Backend — P0/P1

- **P0 — Make slices virtual until finalize.** Every inspected BMS workflow ultimately creates numbered WAVs or other rendered assets, with explicit reports of large file counts and file-manager slowdown. A `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` object removes the export/import boundary during drafting. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) [BMS guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make2)
- **P0 — Deterministic timing plus round-trip validation.** BMSE rounding to 192th can differ from iBMSC arbitrary-resolution data; current failure modes include missing keysounds and gamemode changes after save. Validate both raw and target-format positions before export and provide a round-trip test. [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
- **P1 — Guard duplicate/overlapping events.** A user reports silent MIDI export crashes on overlapping notes and recommends duplicate deletion, sometimes followed by another editor’s re-save. Detect, explain, and offer merge/reuse rather than failing silently. [User report](https://note.com/soramizawakana/n/n98560efdc58d)
- **P1 — Model playback policy explicitly.** Legacy DJMAX behavior could cut off an earlier sample on the same track; TECHNIKA 2 reportedly removed mutual interference. The backend should expose overlap policy per target mode rather than assuming all engines behave alike. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer — keep these

1. **Keep Woslicer’s low-latency marker editing and preview loop:** keyboard placement, grid movement, preview, and one-command batch export are why the basic interaction is still effective. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)
2. **Keep Sayaslicer’s explicit dual clipboard targets:** BMSE’s safe 192th rounding and iBMSC’s arbitrary-resolution path serve different compatibility needs; expose the consequence instead of hiding it. [Sayaslicer features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
3. **Keep Sayaslicer’s project persistence, undo/redo, copy/paste markers, drag/drop, offset, tail remover, fadeout, and zero-cross controls.** These directly address the otherwise destructive export cycle. [Sayaslicer features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
4. **Keep Woslicer III/BMHelper’s MIDI-assisted reduction path, but make it native:** the reason to reduce keysounds is demonstrated by BMHelper and sound-slicer melodic mode. [BMHelper](https://github.com/zardoru/bmhelper) [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)

## 4. Top 10 DJMax Studio recommendations

1. **P0: Virtual-slice project model.** Store source identity, start/end milliseconds, source hash, and per-slice overrides; render WAV/OGG only on Finalize. This directly eliminates the numbered-file/export ceremony documented in Woslicer and community workflows. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) [BMS guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make2)
2. **P0: Dual timeline.** Put waveform and millisecond ruler below, chart preview and bar/beat/quantized ruler above, with one synchronized playhead. The need follows from BPM matching and the difference between iBMSC arbitrary timing and BMSE 192th rounding. [Woslicer III guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
3. **P0: Import to Studio / round-trip validator.** Import BMS/iBMSC/BMSE clipboard and re-export a validated target; show every timing rounding, missing reference, duplicate, and definition overflow before commit. [iBMSC issue](https://github.com/zardoru/iBMSC/issues/5) [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
4. **P1: Slice Library with deduplication.** List each virtual slice, usages, waveform thumbnail, tail policy, and whether it is unique or reused; provide “reuse identical” and “new copy.” Sound-slicer demonstrates the cost difference between 1,000 per-event slices and 10 reused melodic slices. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
5. **P1: Per-slice zero-cross, fade, normalize, and tail preview.** Show raw boundary, adjusted boundary, and audible tail; let users override global defaults. This is justified by click reduction versus marker movement and by reports that reverb tails require one-by-one checking. [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/4de2639ea97bc6723650)
6. **P1: Snap modes 1/4–1/192 plus free-ms and explicit quantization preview.** Preserve Sayaslicer’s arbitrary 1/1–1/192 model but add a raw-ms mode; never silently move a zero-cross marker. [Sayaslicer features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
7. **P1: Mode switcher BMS / RESPECT / TECHNIKA.** Each mode should surface definition limits, overlap behavior, lane semantics, and export validation. DJMAX references document 1,023/2,047 limits, legacy interruption, and later non-interfering behavior. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)
8. **P1: Safe overlap and duplicate diagnostics.** Highlight silent duplicate notes, conflicting same-lane overlaps, and “later sample interrupts earlier” risks; offer merge, reuse, BGM, or split-lane actions. [User report](https://note.com/soramizawakana/n/n98560efdc58d) [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)
9. **P2: One-command finalize with manifest and cleanup preview.** Show count, duration, format, channel layout, peak/normalization, expected disk size, names, and unused outputs before rendering; this addresses file-count management and Explorer slowdown. [BMS guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make2)
10. **P2: Keyboard-first, inspectable UX.** Retain Woslicer/Sayaslicer shortcuts, add a command palette and shortcut overlay, and make disabled actions explain their precondition (e.g., missing source filename). [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) [Sayaslicer shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts) [Woslicer III guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
